IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p93#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p93#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p93#2/r9.claim: God made the Quran guidance for the whole community and urged reflection and interpretive effort, as shown by commands to fear God as able, refer matters to qualified authorities, and recognize clear signs in learned hearts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p93#2/r9.anchor: ودعاهم إلى تدبره وبذل الجهد في استخراج معانيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p93#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p93#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p93#2/r10.claim: Scholars agree the Quran is authoritative for Islamic law, while they dispute transmitted reports over authentication criteria and uneven access; the Quran is their strongest common reference in disagreement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p93#2/r10.anchor: على أن القرآن هو الحجة العامة بين علماء الإسلام لا يختلفون في كونه حجة شريعتهم وإن اختلفوا في حجية ما عداه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r1.claim: The author favors deriving shayṭān from shatana, to be distant, since Satan is far from good and God's mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r1.anchor: فقال الحذاق: «هو فيعال من شطن إذا بعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r2.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line uses nawā shaṭūn for a distant journey, supporting the derivation of shayṭān from distance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r2.anchor:
قال الأعشى: [الوافر] .
نأت بسعاد عنك نوى شطون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r3.claim: Another group derives shayṭān from shāṭa, to blaze or burn, on the pattern faʿlān, because those are its deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: إن شيطانا مأخوذ من شاط يشيط إذا هاج وأحرق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the burning etymology: Sibawayh's tashayṭana means acting satanically, a form that points to shatana rather than shāṭa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r4.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: ويرد على هذه الفرقة أن سيبويه حكى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r5.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r5.claim: A line by Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt contains shāṭin from shatana, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers as further evidence against the alternative derivation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r5.anchor: ويرد أيضا عليهم بيت أمية بن أبي الصلت: [الخفيف] .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r6.claim: Rajīm is an intensive passive form meaning stoned, here by curse, hatred, and deprivation of mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r6.anchor: وأما الرجيم فهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r7.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r7.claim: Al-Mahdawī reports reader consensus on voicing the istiʿādha at the start of al-Fātiḥa, except that Ḥamza recites it silently.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r7.anchor: قال المهدوي رحمه الله: «أجمع القراء على إظهار الاستعاذة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r8.speaker: المسيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r8.claim: Al-Musayyab reports that the people of Medina began recitation with the basmala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p59/r8.anchor: وروى المسيب عن أهل المدينة أنهم كانوا يفتتحون القراءة بالبسملة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r1.claim: ʿA'isha reports that when the Prophet heard a man reciting at night, he prayed for him because he had reminded him of a passage; a variant says the Prophet had omitted or forgotten it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: لقد سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يقرأ في المسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports the Prophet's instruction not to say “I forgot such-and-such a verse,” but rather that one was made to forget it; Muslim and al-Nasa'i transmit it, with Abu Yaʿla giving a lighter vocalization.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says involuntary forgetting is no deficiency after diligence; the hadith teaches careful wording because forgetting itself is not one's act, though neglect can cause it, and one should not attribute it to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r3.anchor: دليل على أن حصول النسيان للشخص ليس بنقص له إذا كان بعد الاجتهاد والحرص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r4.claim: Although 18:24 attributes forgetting to a person, Ibn Kathir explains it figuratively: the result is named while its cause is intended, since forgetting may arise from sin or neglect.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r4.anchor: وقد أسند النسيان إلى العبد في قوله:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r5.claim: Citing al-Dahhak, Ibn Kathir says remembering God drives Satan from the heart as the call to prayer does; a good deed removes sin, the cause of forgetting vanishes, and remembrance follows.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p75/r5.anchor: لأن النسيان إنما يكون عن سبب قد يكون ذنبا، كما تقدم عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، فأمر الله تعالى بذكره ليذهب الشيطان عن القلب

BAQILLANI:v1p277/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r1.claim: A speaker’s character can show through imitation or artificial speech, revealing what he meant to conceal and making his words convey the opposite of his display.
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r1.anchor: وقد يصدر عن المتشبه ويخرج عن المتصنع فيعرف من حاله ما ظن انه يخفيه

BAQILLANI:v1p277/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r2.claim: Al-Mutanabbī’s “horses, night, wilderness know me” has greater emotional force because he is known for courage than al-Buḥturī’s claim that his stance and swords testify to his bravery.
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r2.anchor: فالخيل والليل والبيداء تعرفني والحرب والضرب والقرطاس والقلم

BAQILLANI:v1p277/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r3.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s boasts fit his lineage and persona, giving them force that would repel if voiced by someone else; Abū Firās’s raid and battle boasts provide another fitting example.
BAQILLANI:v1p277/r3.anchor: فانظر في القصيدة كلها ثم في جميع شعره تعلم انه ملك الشعر وانه يليق به من الفخر خاصة

BURHAN:v3p446/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p446/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p446/r1.claim: ربك primes the later ربّه for a double meaning: it can mean God or the king, whereas ربّه alone would indicate only God.
BURHAN:v3p446/r1.anchor: فإن لفظة ربك رشحت لفظة ربه لأن يكون تورية إذ يحتمل أنه أراد بها الإله سبحانه والملك

BURHAN:v4p36/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p36/r10.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v4p36/r10.claim: One interpretation makes both pronouns refer to Joseph: he asked the rescued man to tell the king about his case, and Satan made Joseph forget his Lord.
BURHAN:v4p36/r10.anchor: قيل الضميران عائدان على يوسف قال للناجي ذكر الملك بأمري

BURHAN:v4p36/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p36/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p36/r13.claim: ذكر can mean a reminder or the verbal noun of mentioning; the phrase means Satan made him forget Joseph's mention before his lord, with mention attached to God only by semantic affinity.
BURHAN:v4p36/r13.anchor: والذكر على هذا يحتمل وجهين إن يكون بمعنى التذكير ويكون مصدر ذكرته ذكرا

ITQAN:v4p387/r32.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p387/r32.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p387/r32.claim: The person Joseph thought would be saved from the two prisoners is the cupbearer.
ITQAN:v4p387/r32.anchor: ﴿ للذي ظن أنه ناج ﴾ هو الساقي

ITQAN:v2p415/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p415/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p415/r6.claim: In Joseph's request, dhikr means speaking to the king or telling him Joseph's situation.
ITQAN:v2p415/r6.anchor: والحديث ﴿ اذكرني عند ربك ﴾ أي حدثه بحالي

ITQAN:v4p388/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p388/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p388/r1.claim: The king meant by at your lord is Rayyan ibn al-Walid.
ITQAN:v4p388/r1.anchor: ﴿ عند ربك ﴾ هو الملك ريان بن الوليد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r1.claim: Fronting the subject in affirmative reports strengthens promises and guarantees, where the listener may doubt fulfillment, and strengthens praise and boasting by forestalling doubt.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r1.anchor: أن من شأن من تعده وتضمن له أن يعترضه الشك في تمام الوعد وفي الوفاء به ، فهو من أحوج شيء إلى التأكيد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r2.claim: When an action is expected and undisputed, Arabic normally reports it with the verb first, such as قد خرج or قد ركب, rather than foregrounding the subject.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r2.anchor: قلت : قد خرج . ولم تحتج إلى أن تقول : هو قد خرج ،

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r3.claim: In circumstantial clauses, word order changes emphasis: subject-first wording makes a late arrival more reproachable, while saying someone came before sunrise more strongly marks haste.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r3.anchor: أفلا ترى أنك إذا استبطأت إنسانا فقلت : أتانا والشمس قد طلعت ، كان ذلك أبلغ في استبطائك له

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r4.claim: The source says an unfronted construction with the sun not yet risen is awkward here; eloquent phrasing begins with the subject and builds the verb on it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p114/r4.anchor: هذا وهو كلام لا يكاد يجيء إلا نابيا ، وإنما الكلام البليغ هو أن تبدأ بالاسم ، وتبني الفعل عليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r1.claim: أجاءك رجل asks whether any man came at all; it uses verb-first order because the question is about the occurrence of an arrival, not the visitor’s identity or kind.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r1.anchor: إذا قلت : أجاءك رجل ؟ فأنت تريد أن تسأله : هل كان مجيء من أحد من الرجال إليه ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r2.claim: أرجل جاءك asks whether the already-known visitor was a man or a woman; putting the noun first asks about the agent’s kind.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r2.anchor: فإن قدمت الاسم فقلت : أرجل جاءك ؟ فأنت تسأله عن جنس من جاءه أرجل هو أم امرأة ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r3.claim: An indefinite noun cannot be fronted when neither an individual nor a known category is intended, because subject-first order asks about the agent’s identity or kind.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r3.anchor: كان محالا أن تقدم الاسم النكرة ، وأنت لا تريد السؤال عن الجنس ، لأنه لا يكون لسؤالك حينئذ متعلق

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r4.claim: Modifiers can specify the category or identity being asked about: أرجل طويل asks tall or short, while a relative clause can distinguish a familiar giver from a stranger.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r4.anchor: فإن قلت : أرجل طويل جاءك أم قصير ؟ كان السؤال عن أن الجائي من جنس طوال الرجال أم قصارهم ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r5.claim: In a statement, رجل جاءني is apt only when correcting a belief about the visitor’s gender or category; otherwise the normal order is جاءني رجل.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r5.anchor: حتى تريد أن تعلمه أن الذي جاءك رجل لا امرأة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r6.claim: In the proverb شر أهر ذا ناب, شر is fronted to identify the cause as evil rather than good, matching the sense of ما أهر ذا ناب إلا شر.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r6.anchor: وقولهم : ' شر أهر ذا ناب ' إنما قدم فيه ' شر ' لأن المراد أن يعلم أن الذي أهر ذا الناب هو من جنس الشر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r7.claim: Negation with إلا restricts an action to one known possibility and denies the rest; ما أتاني إلا رجل is appropriate only if the listener might think a woman came.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p119/r7.anchor: فإذا قلت : ما جاءني إلا زيد ؛ كان المعنى أنك قد قصرت المجيء على زيد ، ونفيته عن كل من عداه وإنما يتصور قصر الفعل على معلوم .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p256/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p256/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p256/r3.claim: إنما affirms an action for one person and denies that same action of another at once; جاءني زيد لا عمرو presents the two ideas in sequence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p256/r3.anchor: اعلم أنها تفيد في الكلام بعدها إيجاب الفعل لشيء ، ونفيه عن غيره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p256/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p256/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p256/r4.claim: A second advantage of إنما is that it makes the named person’s responsibility for the action more explicit than simple coordination with لا.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p256/r4.anchor: وهي أنها تجعل الأمر ظاهرا في أن الجائي زيد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r1.claim: In جاءني زيد لا عمرو, لا removes the particular arrival in question from Amr and assigns it to Zayd; it does not deny that Amr ever came too.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r1.anchor: ألا ترى أن ليس المعنى في قولك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r2.claim: The correction assumes the listener knows that someone came but mistakenly attributes that arrival to Amr; the speaker identifies Zayd as the one who came.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r2.anchor: ونكتة أخرى وهي أنك لا تقول : جاءني زيد لا عمر و ، حتى يكون قد بلغ المخاطب أنه كان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r3.claim: Jurjani extends this analysis to إنما: it corrects who performed the mentioned action without implying that no one accompanied Zayd.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r3.anchor: وإذ قد عرفت هذه المعاني في الكلام

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r4.claim: Reading إنما as explicitly saying Zayd alone came from the whole group is possible only with added wording like وحده; that restriction is contrived in ordinary usage.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p257/r4.anchor: فإن ذلك شيء كالتكلف ، والكلام هو الأول

DAMGHANI:v1p180/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r4.claim: Dhikr can mean mentioning Joseph’s case to the king; the source groups this with God’s instruction to recount Abraham and other prophets.
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r4.anchor: الرابع : الذكر بمعنى اذكر أمري عند فلان قوله عز وجل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r1.claim: Dhikr has two literal senses, remembrance in the heart and remembrance on the tongue, and can be used figuratively when context indicates.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r1.anchor: الذكر يقال على وجهين : - أحدهما : الذكر بالقلب . والثاني : الذكر باللسان . وهو في الموضعين حقيقي ويستعار في مواضع تدل عليها القرينة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r2.speaker: ابن جني
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni distinguishes vocalization: kasra for remembrance by tongue and ḍamma for remembrance by heart.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r2.anchor: عن ابن جني قال الذكر بكسر الذال باللسان وبضم الذال بالقلب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r3.claim: The expression “keep this in mind” uses dhikr with ḍamma to mean not forgetting.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r3.anchor: ويقال اجعل هذا على ذكر منك بضم الذال ، أي : لا تنسه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r4.claim: Dhikr can also mean exalted rank or honor; mudhakkar can describe a woman who gave birth to a boy.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r4.anchor: والذكر : العلا والشرف . والمذكر : التي ولدت ذكرا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ uses dhakara for male children in asking how many sons someone has.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r5.anchor: قال الفراء : كم الذكرة من ولدك ؟ أي : الذكور .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r6.claim: The first Qur'anic face is spoken remembrance of God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r6.anchor: أحدها : الذكر باللسان . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r7.claim: A second face is remembrance in the heart, which some explain as regret after sin.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r7.anchor: والثاني : الذكر بالقلب . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران : ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ﴾ ، وقيل هو الندم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r8.claim: A third face is reporting or telling someone about a matter; Joseph asks the released cupbearer to tell the king about him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r8.anchor: والثالث : الحديث . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في يوسف ] : - ﴿ اذكرني عند ربك ﴾ ، أي : حدثه بحالي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r9.claim: A fourth face is a report or account, as in the accounts of earlier prophets and peoples.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r9.anchor: والرابع : الخبر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف : ^ ( قل سأتلوا عليكم منه ذكرا ) ^ ، وفي الأنبياء : ﴿ هذا ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r10.claim: A fifth face is admonition or reminder, as in passages addressing those who ignore warnings.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p301/r10.anchor: والخامس : العظة . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في الأنعام : ^ ( فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء ) ^ )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r1.claim: Shayṭān names any rebellious being; Abu ʿUbayda includes rebellious jinn, humans, and animals.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r1.anchor: الشيطان : اسم لكل متمرد . قال أبو عبيدة معمر بن المثنى : كل غالب متمرد من الجن والإنس والدواب فهو شيطان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r2.claim: Scholars disagree whether the nūn is radical or an added letter.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r2.anchor: واختلف العلماء هل نون الشيطان أصلية أم زائدة على قولين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r3.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r3.claim: The first view derives the word from sh-ṭ-n, “to be distant”; a poem by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt supports the radical nūn.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أن النون فيه أصلية كأنه من شطن ، أي : بعد . يقال من ذلك : شطنت داره

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r4.claim: On that derivation, one explanation is that the devil is so named for being far from goodness; another is his deep distance in evil.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r4.anchor: فعلى هذا القول فإنه مأخوذ من شطن وفي تسميته بذلك قولان : - أحدهما : أنه سمي شيطانا لبعده عن الخير . والثاني : لبعد غوره في الشر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r5.claim: The alternative derives it from sh-ya-ṭ, meaning to perish; on this view, the name reflects destruction through sin.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن النون فيه زائدة فيكون من شاط يشيط إذا ذهب وهلك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r6.claim: A poem supports the alternative root meaning of perishing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r6.anchor: وأنشدوا من ذلك : - وقد يشيط على أرماحنا البطل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r7.claim: One Qur'anic face is the leaders or soothsayers whom unbelievers consult in private.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r7.anchor: أحدها : الكاهن . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم ﴾ ، وقيل : هم رؤساؤهم في الكفر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r8.claim: A second face is a rebellious being among jinn or humans.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r8.anchor: والثاني : الطاغي من الجن والإنس . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r9.claim: A third face is a snake, as in the description of the tree's fruit in Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r9.anchor: والثالث : الحية . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات : ^ ( طلعها كأنه رؤوس الشياطين )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r10.claim: A fourth face identifies the devil with Umayya ibn Khalaf; another view says Abu Jahl, while “the human” is ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayṭ.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p374/r10.anchor: والرابع : أمية بن خلف . ومنه قوله تعالى في الفرقان : ^ ( وكان الشيطان للإنسان خذولا ) ^ ، وقيل : أريد بالشيطان ها هنا أبو جهل . وبالإنسان عقبة بن أبي معيط
